surprises.description: Brown & Brown reported $1.7 billion of revenue, below the preview’s $1.76 billion consensus estimate. Revenue grew 7.4%, also slower than the preview’s implied 9.8% year-over-year growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q3 FY2026 Consensus | $1.76B”; the preview says consensus implies “~+9.8%.”

surprises.description: Organic revenue excluding contingents grew 1.2%, 0.7 percentage points below the +1.9% consensus that the preview identified as the central hurdle. Including contingents, organic growth was 1.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic revenue grew only 1.2% (1.5% including contingents), reflecting significant pricing headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic revenue (ex-contingents) | +1.9%”; the preview calls this “the entire print.”

surprises.description: Specialty Distribution organic growth was -0.8%, missing management’s previously guided +2% to +4% range by a wide margin. The call attributed the decline to carriers reclaiming E&S business, earthquake pricing pressure, delayed loan-portfolio onboarding, and weak flood claims revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Distribution organic growth declined 0.8%, missing the previously guided +2% to +4% range,” due to the listed business and market factors.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management’s Specialty Distribution organic range was “+2% to +4%” and notes that management “guided to a 2–4% recovery here.”

surprises.description: The forward outlook for Specialty was weaker than the preview’s expected 2H range being reiterated: management now expects a 2%–4% Q4 decline, including $8 million–$12 million of nonrecurring and timing-related headwinds, and only 1%–3% organic growth in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Distribution 2027 organic guidance is just 1%-3%, with an expected Q4 2026 decline of 2%-4% including $8M-$12M of nonrecurring and timing-related headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management’s 2H Specialty range was “2–4%” and its base case expected “2H ranges reiterated”; it also anticipated “no 2027 commitment.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.07, below the preview’s $1.08–$1.09 consensus range. EPS growth was also 1.9%, below the preview’s cited consensus growth of 2.9%–3.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $1.08–$1.09”; the preview gives expected growth of “+2.9%–3.8%.”

surprises.description: Retail organic growth reached 2.6%, slightly above management’s prior 1.5%–2.5% range, and the company raised its Q4 retail outlook to 2%–3% and set 2027 guidance at 2%–4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail outperformed with 2.6% organic growth, and management raised Q4 retail guidance to 2%-3% and set 2027 retail organic guidance at 2%-4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists management’s Retail range as “+1.5% to +2.5%” and says its base case assumes “Retail in the guided band”; it expected “no 2027 commitment.”

surprises.description: Management raised its Accession synergy targets: 2026 synergies are now about $50 million rather than $30 million–$40 million, and the 2028 run-rate net EBITDAC target rose to $175 million from $150 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 Accession synergy estimate to approximately $50 million (from $30M-$40M) and increased its 2028 run-rate net EBITDAC synergy target to $175 million (from $150M).”

surprises.description: Alongside the higher synergy targets, the company raised its integration-cost estimate to $250 million–$300 million and cited an additional $90 million of prefunded debt-like items, a cost burden the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised “integration cost estimates to $250M-$300M plus an additional $90M of prefunded debt-like items.”

surprises.description: Management said Q4 adjusted EBITDAC margins will again be down year over year, signaling another period of margin pressure after the preview cited FY26 guidance of roughly flat margins excluding lower investment income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided that Q4 margins will again be down year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview quotes FY26 guidance as “roughly flat… excluding the effect of lower investment income.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed further Specialty Distribution commission pressure beyond the weak organic outlook: contingent commissions are expected to fall $14 million–$16 million year over year in Q4, with additional pressure expected in 2027 as program profitability shrinks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Distribution contingent commissions are expected to decline $14M-$16M year-over-year in Q4 2026, with further downward pressure anticipated in 2027 as program profitability shrinks.”

surprises.description: The call quantified severe pricing declines in E&S property, with rates down 15%–35%, and forecast a further 10%–20% industry-wide decline in CAT property rates in 2027. The preview had flagged soft property pricing and CAT exposure, but these figures make the pressure more pronounced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “E&S property rates fell 15%-35% and CAT property rates are expected to drop an estimated 10%-20% industry-wide in 2027, pressuring Specialty's catastrophe-exposed lines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flags “CAT property” exposure and cites the market index showing “property -10%”; it says soft-market pressure is real.
